item.text:
**Overall**
Kishida’s 2024 record leans **yes** on 6B.2, but in a concentrated way: the clearest evidence is for **child support, housing, disaster relief, school/childcare subsidies, and targeted social protection for low-income households and vulnerable people**. The weakest area is **water/sanitation**, where I found no direct 2024 policy evidence. The main counterevidence is that **household purchasing power and real wages still deteriorated**, so access gains were real but incomplete.

**Positive**
- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html)  
  Kishida put **child allowance expansion, reduced higher-education costs, daycare staffing improvements, and additional childcare support** at the center of the 2024 agenda, and tied funding to expenditure reform rather than new household burdens.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida on the Package of Measures to Support the Daily Lives and the Livelihoods of the Disaster Victims and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-25 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html)  
  The package included **cash aid, emergency housing, support for demolished homes, reduced medical/nursing-care burdens, help with school visits, and tax measures**, with explicit attention to **low-income households, healthcare, childcare, schools, transit, SMEs, agriculture, and tourism**.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `6B.1`

- **Policies supporting children and child-rearing** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html)  
  The cabinet page states the government would expand **child allowances**, reduce **childbirth and higher-education burdens**, increase **housing support for child-rearing households**, improve **prenatal/postnatal care**, and strengthen **early-childhood education and childcare**.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`

- **Video Message from Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio on International Women’s Day** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-03-08 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html)  
  Kishida linked women’s empowerment to **gender equality, wage parity, executive appointments, work-family balance, and anti-sexual-violence protections**, all framed as conditions for a society where people can live with peace of mind.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `4B.7`

- **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-04-19 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html)  
  Kishida said regional revitalization mattered for national development and pushed **sustainable local services, digital tools, and grants**, which supports geographically broader access to public services rather than Tokyo-centered concentration.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html)  
  Kishida said expanded subsidies would reduce burdens for **school lunches, agriculture, SMEs, medical and nursing care, childcare, school facilities, public baths, public transport, logistics, and regional tourism**, and that energy subsidies were meant to cushion **low-income households**.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`

- **July 3 apology and redress for forced sterilization victims** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-03 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html)  
  Kishida called the former Eugenics Protection Law unconstitutional, offered **sincere remorse**, and promised **compensation and new guarantees**, which is direct welfare-oriented redress for a grave state harm.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `4B.7`, `5B.5`

- **Noto Peninsula earthquake response instructions** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-01 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html)  
  Kishida ordered **warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency response with human life first**, showing welfare protection as an immediate governing priority in crisis.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.9`, `6B.1`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-11 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html)  
  He emphasized **secondary evacuation for vulnerable groups** and prioritized avoiding disease, congestion, and winter hazards, which is concrete protection of life and health.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.9`, `4B.7`

**Mixed / Negative**
- **Japan's Dec real wages, household spending fall again** | Reuters | 2024-02-05 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japans-dec-real-wages-household-spending-fall-again-3293300)  
  Real wages fell for a 21st straight month and household spending declined again, showing that Kishida had not yet translated wage policy into improved purchasing power or broader access to goods and services.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- **Japan warns of weak yen impact on households in government white paper** | Reuters | 2024-08-01 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-warns-of-weak-yen-impact-on-households-in-government-white-paper-3551065)  
  The government itself said a weak yen was hurting household sentiment and could erode purchasing power, a clear sign that living-condition pressures remained severe despite support measures.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- **Japan's govt to warn of weak yen pain in policy roadmap, draft shows** | Reuters | 2024-06-03 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/japans-govt-to-warn-of-weak-yen-pain-in-policy-roadmap-draft-shows-3469044)  
  Reuters reported the roadmap would warn of weak-yen pain for households and that consumption was stalling, which limits any claim that 2024 produced a clearly better material-welfare environment.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- **Inquiry Needed into Japan’s Flawed Criminal Justice System** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-04 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/04/inquiry-needed-japans-flawed-criminal-justice-system)  
  This is not a welfare-policy page, but it is negative structural context: HRW says Japan still had abusive detention and weak correction mechanisms, so Kishida did not fix all rights-protecting public institutions in 2024.  
  QIDs: `6B.2`, `4B.10`, `4B.7`

**Search gap**
- I found **strong direct evidence** on child allowances, schooling, childcare, housing, disaster relief, low-income subsidies, and medical/nursing-care burdens.
- I found **little to no direct 2024 evidence** on **water/sanitation** or a broad nationwide **health-system expansion** beyond targeted care subsidies and disaster-related support.
- I also found no strong 2024 evidence of a major new **food-security** program separate from agricultural/price-relief measures.
